subject: science

entries: A mole is a counting word - one dozen is 12 eggs and one mole is 6.02 × 10²³ particles, far too many to count one by one, so we weigh moles instead of counting them.
slots.label: A mole is a counting word
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Mass to moles - the mass of one mole of carbon-12 is 12 g, its molar mass, so weighing 12 g of carbon gives exactly one mole with n = m / M.
slots.label: Mass to moles
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Mole ratios - balanced equations count moles, not grams: 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O gives the fixed 2 : 1 : 2 ratio, and doubling one reactant doubles the others.
slots.label: Mole ratios
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: one mole of everything weighs the same - one mole always has the same number of particles but a different mass, because each substance has its own molar mass.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A counting word for 6.02 × 10²³ particles, just as a dozen is a counting word for 12 items. Chemists weigh moles instead of counting particles one by one.
slots.label: Mole
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The mass of one mole of a substance, in grams per mole (g/mol). Carbon-12 is 12 g/mol, hydrogen is 1 g/mol and oxygen is 16 g/mol.
slots.label: Molar mass
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The number of particles in one mole: 6.02 × 10²³. Every mole of any substance contains this many particles.
slots.label: Avogadro constant
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: How heavy a sample is, in grams. Mass links to moles through mass = moles x molar mass, or n = m / M.
slots.label: Mass
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: A single atom, molecule or ion being counted. A mole counts particles without saying which kind - the kind decides the molar mass.
slots.label: Particle
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The ratio of moles in a balanced equation, such as 2 : 1 : 2 for 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O. It scales as a whole when amounts change.
slots.label: Mole ratio
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: The mole: counting atoms by weighing
